title: The DOJ is investigating a16z. What does this mean for venture capital?
content:
Andreessen Horowitz has two partners sitting on the boards of companies that now compete with each other: Ben Horowitz at Databricks and Martin Casado at Fivetran. Nothing too scandalous on the surface, except the Department of Justice has reportedly been investigating the arrangement for almost a year, dusting off a 112-year-old antitrust law that’s rarely used against VCs.
Board conflicts aren’t exactly new, and these companies weren’t necessarily direct competitors when a16z first invested in them. But as portfolio companies expand into each other’s markets, the DOJ’s scrutiny raises a much bigger question for venture firms: How do you manage board seats when the boundaries between your portfolio companies keep moving? 
 
On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Anthony Ha, and Sean O’Kane dig into the a16z probe, what it could mean for VCs, and more of the week’s headlines. 
Listen to the full episode to hear more about:
- Why Stripe paid $7.5 billion for AI model router OpenRouter, and why the “singularity” isn’t the real reason
- What happens to the AI companies caught in the middle as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia pull further ahead
- Why Rivian spinout Also just raised $150 million to make a bigger bet on autonomous vehicles
- Uber’s newest delivery partnership with drone company Zipline, and what it means for the other autonomous startups betting their futures on Uber
- Whether we’ve reached peak valuation for AI dictation apps after Wispr’s $280 million raise at a $2 billion valuation

report.summary: 美司法部罕见调查a16z董事席位冲突，风投行业或面临新监管压力。
report.background: Andreessen Horowitz（a16z）两位合伙人分别担任Databricks和Fivetran的董事，随着这两家投资组合公司业务扩张，逐渐形成竞争关系。美国司法部据报已就此调查近一年，并援引一部112年前的反垄断法——该法极少用于风险投资机构。此事触及风投行业的普遍痛点：投资机构通常在多家潜在竞争公司董事会拥有席位，过去被视为常态，但监管风向可能正在转变。若司法部胜诉，将重塑风投参与公司治理的方式。
key_points: a16z合伙人同时担任Databricks和Fivetran董事，而这两家公司如今在数据领域存在竞争，引发利益冲突质疑。
司法部引用1914年《克莱顿反垄断法》第8条，该条款禁止同一个人同时在竞争公司董事会任职，但很少针对风投基金。
a16z最初投资时两家公司并非直接对手，但随着各自扩展业务边界，原本清晰的赛道划分变得模糊，暴露了VC的固有风险。
此案可能开创先例：未来风投机构在安排董事席位时，需更谨慎评估投资组合公司间的潜在竞争关系。
风投行业整体将面临压力，可能需要重构管理合伙人董事任职的合规流程，甚至考虑放弃部分董事会席位。
report.impact: 对AI和科技行业而言，这标志着监管机构开始关注资本通过董事会交叉持股可能形成的市场控制力，后续AI领域竞争性投资可能面临更多审查。对创业者来说，选择风投时可能要评估其多家被投公司间的潜在冲突，避免未来被卷入反垄断纠纷。对普通用户，长期看有助于维持市场公平竞争，防止少数资本通过董事会渗透扭曲创新方向，但短期内可能减缓部分科技公司的扩张速度。
report.tools: 关注该事件的读者可参考Carta（董事会管理工具）理解董事席位流程，PitchBook或Crunchbase（风险投资数据库）追踪a16z投资组合动态；如需了解美国反垄断执法进展，可关注FTC和DOJ反垄断局官方网站的公告及案例更新。
